correctness.rationale: Gamma–Dirichlet normalization gives intrinsic-uniform probability on the simplex, and sorting exchangeable column-pair differences gives the exact conditional Monge measure. An explicit Jacobian separates each exponential pair into independent Laplace difference and exponential minimum. Row sums stay independent Gamma totals, yielding Beta(n,n). For one common infinite coupling, empirical Laplace quantiles converge in L1 and weighted empirical marked CDFs converge uniformly; division by S_n/n→2 proves both complete cumulative limit shapes. Joint Laplace extreme CDFs factor asymptotically, and the random denominator changes centered extremes by o_P(1). The exact beta-integral centroid formula follows from gamma sum independence. Standard-library checks corroborate examples, and no infinite theorem depends on numerical sampling.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 paper defines the identical normalized two-row Monge body and proves relative volume \(1/n!\), but the inspected material does not determine the intrinsic-uniform sample law, the complete logarithmic two-row limit profiles, the quarter-mass half-column gap, the exact Beta row-share law, or the independent joint edge-extreme limit. The ordering part of the sampler is an elementary symmetry observation and is not separately claimed to be deep or independently original. The 2019 statistical Monge paper addresses minimax noisy estimation. Published geometric Monge inball and Minkowski-center results concern metric extrema, not volume-random cumulative mass. Source and record searches found no dominating claim; unindexed analogues remain a stated risk.

value.rationale: Intrinsic-uniform geometry is the natural typical-point counterpart to the two-row normalized-volume theorem. A complete pair of logarithmic cumulative mass curves, the exact quarter-mass bias at the median column, the preservation of the Beta row-share law, and independent Gumbel extremes provide a structural bulk-versus-edge classification across all two-row widths. The exact sampler is useful for genuine uniform benchmarking of feasible Monge cost functions. This is not a textbook small-parameter slice or a mere rederivation of the existing volume; it identifies previously unreported natural distributional invariants. No extension to three or more rows is claimed.
